definitions.explanation: The period of Japanese history when the Tokugawa shogunate ruled from Edo (modern-day Tokyo). Characterized by political stability, strict social order, isolationist foreign policy, and flourishing arts and culture.

examples.japanese: {江戸時代|えどじだい}は{約|やく}260{年間|ねんかん}{続|つづ}いた。
examples.english: The Edo period lasted for about 260 years.

examples.japanese: {江戸時代|えどじだい}には{鎖国|さこく}{政策|せいさく}がとられていた。
examples.english: During the Edo period, a policy of national isolation was maintained.

examples.japanese: {江戸時代|えどじだい}に{歌舞伎|かぶき}や{浮世絵|うきよえ}などの{町人|ちょうにん}{文化|ぶんか}が{花開|はなひら}いた。
examples.english: During the Edo period, townspeople's culture such as kabuki and ukiyo-e prints flourished.

notes:
One of the most important periods in Japanese history, spanning from 1603 when {徳川家康|とくがわいえやす} established the shogunate in {江戸|えど} (Edo) to 1868 when the {明治維新|めいじいしん} (Meiji Restoration) returned power to the emperor.

KEY FEATURES:
- {鎖国|さこく}: national isolation policy limiting foreign contact
- {参勤交代|さんきんこうたい}: alternate attendance system requiring feudal lords to spend time in Edo
- {士農工商|しのうこうしょう}: four-class social hierarchy
- Flourishing of {町人|ちょうにん}{文化|ぶんか} (merchant-class culture): {歌舞伎|かぶき}, {浮世絵|うきよえ}, {落語|らくご}

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {江戸時代|えどじだい}の{武士|ぶし}: Edo-period samurai
- {江戸時代|えどじだい}{初期|しょき}/{中期|ちゅうき}/{末期|まっき}: early/mid/late Edo period
- {江戸時代|えどじだい}から{続|つづ}く: continuing since the Edo period

RELATED WORDS:
- {戦国時代|せんごくじだい}: Warring States period — the preceding era of civil war
- {明治時代|めいじじだい}: Meiji period — the following era of modernization
- {徳川幕府|とくがわばくふ}: Tokugawa shogunate — the government of the Edo period
